trend_completeness.comment: min_fraction lowered 0.80 -> 0.60 July 2026 per updated guidelines doc + HISSS manuscript 2.2.3 (overall series gate 60%; first/last-decade gates stay 80%). Language-side fallbacks remain 0.80 (legacy behavior when this section is absent).

snow.comment: Snow metrics from daily SWE (Daymet swe). Days with SWE < swe_day_threshold_mm are treated as snow-free for ALL snow metrics, magnitudes AND durations (domain decision 2026-07-14). seasonal_spell_min_days follows Hatchett (2021) Hydrology 8(1):32 / Petersky & Harpold (2018). Set swe_day_threshold_mm near 0 to reproduce the paper's literal SWE>0 rule. record_anchored_decade_gate (July 2026): the 10 threshold-dependent snow metrics require >= decade_min_fraction (na_handling.trend_completeness — LINKED to the streamflow decade gate) of the SWE-valid years in BOTH the first and last decade of the gage's SWE record to be computable (snowy) before trend statistics are computed; on failure the 6 trend stats are NaN (mean/median + Pettitt still computed); absent key => disabled.

drought.comment: Streamflow drought duration/deficit after Adelsperger et al. (in review), 'A novel severity-based approach for assessing streamflow drought characteristics and drivers'. threshold_percentiles are MAGNITUDE (non-exceedance) percentiles of the 7-day-smoothed flow distribution -- 10 = the flow exceeded 90% of the time -- matching the paper and this repo's Q{n} convention; USDM analogy 30/20/10/5/2 = D0/D1/D2/D3/D4. Thresholds are FIXED (whole record, per run window => record-dependent, matching the paper's per-analysis-period thresholds) and computed with the unbiased Weibull plotting position i/(n+1) (Hyndman-Fan definition 6), NOT the Type-7 default used elsewhere in this repo. The paper's variable day-of-year method is intentionally NOT implemented (user decision 2026-07-27: with one value per calendar day per year, the low levels are very uncertain at 20-46 years and 2% falls below the smallest plotting position 1/(n+1) entirely; below_plotting_range_policy='na' declines to extrapolate there, which is a project policy layered on type 6, not type-6 behaviour - type 6 would clamp to the sample minimum). Aggregation is by WATER year, deviating from the paper's climate year (Apr-Mar). Absent section => family disabled (no drought columns).

high_na_denominator.comment: flagged_for_high_na = (NA or NaN count) / (number of SIGNATURE columns present in the assembled output table) > max_na_fraction. A signature column is any column ending in one of statistic_suffixes, plus the per_gage_scalars registry. Metadata, unregistered diagnostics and flag columns never enter the denominator; families NA-filled by the table union DO count. One manifest shared by Julia, Python and rpkg (2026-09-04; before that each language counted something different and the Julia products counted metadata only).

stats_floor.comment: Minimum non-NA annual values a metric needs before ANY of its 8 statistics (and changepoint fields) are computed; below the floor all are NaN. Applied via the orchestrator to every family EXCEPT recession and elasticity (inherently sparse - same exemption as trend_completeness). Added July 2026 after 4-point Theil-Sen slopes surfaced for clustered snow-timing years (e.g. gage 07292500, snow_on_dowy non-NA only 1982-1985). Absent section => no floor (legacy behavior).

annual_values.comment: Write per-year annual signature values (long-format parquet: gage_id, signature, water_year, value) alongside the summary CSV. Absent section => disabled. Implemented in all three languages (Julia, Python, rpkg) since the August 2026 port campaign.
